goal: What should I verify before applying for this scholarship?

passages.text: Applicants must be bonafide citizens enrolled in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited university. Eligible candidates must have achieved a minimum aggregate of 75% marks in their Higher Secondary Examination (Class 12). Total gross family income from all sources must not exceed INR 4,50,000 per annum.

Candidates are required to upload digital copies of their Class 10 and 12 mark sheets, an official Domicile Certificate issued by a competent magistrate, and an authenticated Income Certificate issued exclusively by the Revenue Officer / Tehsildar or a valid Ration Card.

The online application portal opens on 15 August 2026. The definitive closing date for submitting online applications is 30 November 2026 at 11:59 PM IST. Incomplete submissions or submissions made after the closing date will be rejected automatically without notice.

Selected scholarship recipients will receive a non-repayable grant of INR 50,000 per academic year, transferred directly via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) to the recipient's Aadhaar-seeded bank account in two equal biannual installments.
Applications must be submitted solely through the designated official web portal at https://scholarships.gov.in/national-merit-2026. No physical applications or email submissions will be entertained.

sources.title: StudentDesk: Guide to National Merit Scholarship 2026

passages.text: The National Merit Scholarship provides generous financial aid to undergraduate students. Applicants need to show at least 75% marks in their 12th board exams and must have household income within the Rs 4.5 Lakh ceiling.

Make sure you have your Class 12 passing certificate, student ID card, and bank passbook ready. For financial verification, applicants must upload their parent's formal Income Tax Return (ITR) acknowledgment from the past assessment year or Form 16 from their employer. Revenue certificates without ITR are not accepted on the portal.
The official portal opened in mid-August and the last date for submitting online applications is 30 November 2026.

sources.title: EduTips Blog: Tips for the National Merit Scholarship

passages.text: For the AY 2024-25 cycle, the ministry requires students to maintain a consistent academic record with 75% marks in high school exams. Ensure your college is enrolled under the National Scholarship Portal.
Be aware that the portal for the 2024-25 batch closed in October 2024. Students should always verify whether previous cycle rules carry over to the new term.

sources.title: ScholarshipForum: User Thread on National Merit Application

passages.text: Many students ask whether undergraduate freshers can re-apply if their family income changes later. Note that the official scholarship guidelines discuss initial entry criteria and basic documentation, but do not provide explicit renewal clauses or continuing GPA requirements for year two.
